checks.rationale: 500 paired hotel-days. Below roughly a year of two-hotel coverage the pooled metrics describe a season rather than a year.

40 / 20 / 10 origins at 7 / 14 / 28 days. Windows tile, so the dataset's year of evaluable dates yields about 54 / 27 / 14 origins; each floor sits under that count and was fixed from the arithmetic before any model was fitted. Stage 6.4's 40 is kept where the data can meet it.

zero. A method that declines to forecast some days and is scored only on the rest is being graded on a set it chose; if any day is skipped the result must be read differently, so it fails the gate rather than being averaged over.

one. The final evaluation window is truncated whenever the remaining dates are not a multiple of the step, which is arithmetic rather than a defect. A second incomplete window would mean something else is wrong.
two, which is every hotel in the dataset. This is a completeness check, NOT a generalisation claim: see the model card.
identity: a different contract is a different question.
identity: the feature contract must be the one measured.
identity by content: this horizon's own horizon-matched dataset, whose digest the frozen protocol records. A dataset built at another horizon hashes differently.
the horizon this model was declared for. A different horizon admits a different feature set and a different baseline, and produces numbers that are not comparable.
the horizon's candidate. A mismatch must stop the run rather than validate another horizon's model under this one's name.
two full evaluations of the same bytes must agree exactly, predictions and content checksum alike. Without this nothing else in the record can be reproduced.
every fold's chronology, every window's disjointness and every selected feature's lead time, re-checked on this run rather than inherited from the last one.
MAE, RMSE and sMAPE must all be present for both methods. A missing metric is a measurement that did not happen, not a zero.

excluded_criteria.learned_model_beats_baseline: NOT a criterion. Acceptance here asks whether the measurement is trustworthy, not which method won. The learned model leads on a bare majority of folds with a pooled gap far smaller than the fold-to-fold spread, so such a gate would encode a coin flip. It is also structurally impossible: AcceptanceEvidence carries no metric value.
excluded_criteria.metric_threshold: NOT a criterion. No MAE, RMSE or sMAPE ceiling is declared, because no operational requirement exists to derive one from. A number invented here would become a 'target accuracy' the moment it was written down.

cross_hotel_claim: NONE. Both hotels appear in the training data at every origin; there is no held-out hotel and, with two, there could not be a meaningful one. The per-hotel numbers say the result is not driven by one of them, and say nothing about a third.

errors.ordering: absolute error descending, then target date, then hotel key
errors.signed_error_definition: forecast - actual; positive means the method predicted more demand than was realised
errors.treatment: diagnostic only; no observation was removed, clipped, winsorised or altered, and no model configuration was changed in response

generation.note: Wall-clock and toolchain metadata only, outside the content checksum: re-running the pipeline must not look like a different result.

purpose: descriptive robustness analysis of the 14-day backtest under multi_horizon_v1; no method is ranked, no regime is labelled good or bad, no horizon is compared with another, and no model configuration was changed

2016-08.reason: insufficient coverage; no metric is reported for this group

stability.stdev_definition: population standard deviation over the evaluated folds; these folds are the whole population the protocol produces, not a sample from a larger one
